long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Baku, Farkhad Akhmedov began his business career selling Russian sable pelts on the London commodity exchange. In 1987 he founded Tansley Trading, which supplied equipment to Russian gas producers. He then acquired shares in Nortgas, bought out Bechtel Energy's 44% holding and became chairman, turning an equipment-trading foothold into control of a Siberian natural-gas producer.

Akhmedov sold his remaining 49% Nortgas stake to Novatek in 2012 for $1.375 billion. Forbes now describes his source of wealth as investments and classifies him as self-made, reflecting his shift from operating gas assets to managing the sale proceeds. His later activities include a pomegranate-juice venture in Azerbaijan and the Nar Gallery, formed around his collection of Azerbaijani painting. These projects preserve a business and cultural connection to his birthplace.
